requirements.requirement: On node1, require new user passwords to be at least 12 characters long.
requirements.summary: The installed pwquality policy sets minlen=12, PAM password stacks reference pam_pwquality, and both before and after restart an 11-character, four-class password was rejected specifically for being shorter than 12 characters.

requirements.requirement: On node1, require new user passwords to use at least three different character classes.
requirements.summary: The policy sets minclass=3, PAM consumes pam_pwquality, and both before and after restart a 12-character, one-class password was rejected for having fewer than three classes while a four-class password was accepted.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained AlmaLinux 9.6 with kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6 before and after execution. The implementation used the already-installed EL9 PAM/libpwquality stack, and package health remained clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The password policy is configured, behaviorally validated, connected to PAM, and preserved across a verified restart. The provider-wide restart protocol for node1 is complete: healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement and disconnect, changed boot identity, and recovered system, SSH, policy checksum, and enforcement are directly shown and corroborated by lifecycle snapshots.
limitations: Enforcement was tested with pwscore rather than by performing an actual user password-change transaction through passwd/PAM. The PAM references and matching rejection behavior provide strong supporting evidence, but this keeps confidence below 1.

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed state-changing actions had clear purposes: cmd-89108cfdb40940f0 created the required policy, while cmd-0f4eda3e663a49b8 performed the mandatory restart protocol. No unnecessary mutation was identified. The reboot-related PID and systemd-private-directory changes are expected lifecycle effects; no failed services, new listening endpoints, package damage, or unrelated residue appeared.
